c.tagline: Africa's cleanest, safest capital, set across a thousand green hills.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are typically negotiated or fixed in advance rather than metered; official taxi stands post reference rates, and airport-to-city runs commonly run about $15-20.

emergency.note: 112 is the general police/emergency line; 912 reaches SAMU ambulance services. Tourist assistance can also be reached via the Rwanda Development Board hotline.

avoid.reason: Very safe and clean; usual petty-crime caution. Border areas with DR Congo — check advisories

hood_desc: A leafy hillside district above downtown with embassies, colonial-era buildings and the historic Hotel des Mille Collines; suits travelers who want boutique charm within walking distance of the center.
The compact downtown core on Nyarugenge Hill with banks, markets, casinos and budget-to-midrange hotels; good for budget travelers and those who want to be in the middle of city life.

A modern, hilly district anchored by the Kigali Convention Centre, packed with embassies, international hotel chains, and trendy restaurants and bars; ideal for conference-goers, business travelers and expats.

An affluent, quiet suburb built around the city's only golf course, with gated villas and leafy streets; suits business travelers, golfers and families wanting a residential feel away from downtown bustle.

Kigali's most vibrant and colorful neighborhood, nicknamed the 'Muslim Quarter,' known for walking tours, local eateries and budget guesthouses; suits backpackers and travelers wanting an authentic cultural experience.
lodging: Radisson Blu Hotel & Convention Centre Kigali

water.note: Treated in modern plants but old pipes risk contamination; bottled water is the safer choice for visitors.

transit.pay: Most city buses use the smartcard-based 'Tap&Go' e-ticketing system; cards are bought and topped up at kiosks or via mobile money. Moto-taxis and regular taxis are paid in cash (Rwandan francs) or increasingly via mobile money/ride-hailing apps.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30/6:00 AM to 9:00/10:00 PM with limited late-night service; moto-taxis and taxis operate around the clock as the main after-hours option.
transit.note: Kigali has no rail or metro system; minibus/coach buses and motorcycle taxis (moto-taxis) are the backbone of public transport, supplemented by ride-hailing apps like Yego Cab.

tip.r: Not traditionally customary but increasingly appreciated; rounding up or adding 5-10% at restaurants is welcome, especially where no service charge is included.
